model_name: Mechanistic Model of Hantavirus Zoonotic Transmission

deer_mouse.description: Exposed (infected but not yet infectious) male and female rodents
Infective (chronically infected and shedding virus) male and female rodents
Recovered male and female rodents (assumed to have lifelong immunity)

human.description: Exposed humans (incubation period, not yet infectious)
Infective humans (symptomatic phase, capable of transmission for certain viruses)
Recovered humans (survived infection and are now immune)

transmission_pathways: Infective Male Rodent -> Susceptible Male Rodent (beta_m)
Infective Female Rodent -> Susceptible Male Rodent (beta_f)
Infective Male Rodent -> Susceptible Female Rodent (beta_mf)
Infective Female Rodent -> Susceptible Female Rodent (beta_f)

ecological_factors.description: The presence of less-competent host species (e.g., voles) can reduce hantavirus prevalence in the primary reservoir host population (deer mice).
Events like El Niño can increase precipitation and rodent food supply, leading to rodent population booms and subsequent hantavirus outbreaks in humans with a time lag (approx. 1 year).

rodent_population.description: SEIR model for male and female rodents.
system: dS_m/dt = B/2 - beta_f * I_f * S_m - beta_m * I_m * S_m - d(N) * S_m
dE_m/dt = beta_f * I_f * S_m + beta_m * I_m * S_m - (delta + d(N)) * E_m
dS_f/dt = B/2 - beta_f * I_f * S_f - beta_mf * I_m * S_f - d(N) * S_f
dE_f/dt = beta_f * I_f * S_f + beta_mf * I_m * S_f - (delta + d(N)) * E_f
auxiliary_equations: N = N_m + N_f = (S_m + E_m + I_m + R_m) + (S_f + E_f + I_f + R_f)

human_population.description: SEIR model for human transmission, incorporating zoonotic and potential interhuman routes.
system: dS_h/dt = B_h - beta_rh * (I_m + I_f) * S_h - beta_hh * I_h * S_h - d_h * S_h
dE_h/dt = beta_rh * (I_m + I_f) * S_h + beta_hh * I_h * S_h - (delta_h + d_h) * E_h
dI_h/dt = delta_h * E_h - (gamma_h + d_h + alpha_h) * I_h
